requirement:
`habeas status` MUST display the file, line, and test name for each violation of
{cite}`requirements.references.coverage.tests`. The command MUST exit successfully
when it completes the report with these findings.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.cli.status.test_annotations` has two clauses. (1) `habeas status` "MUST display the file, line, and test name for each violation" of `requirements.references.coverage.tests`. (2) The command "MUST exit successfully when it completes the report with these findings." Both clauses describe output and exit status, which a user can observe. The text names no library, algorithm, signature, type, field or interface that the implementation must use.

I tried an alternative implementation for each clause. A different report renderer, a different data type for violations, or a different place where the findings are computed would print the same file, line and test name and would exit with the same status. All of those choices are discretionary. The same holds for the contextual text. `requirements.references.coverage.tests` and the `requirements.references.test_source_item` definition describe what counts as a violation and how Habeas recognizes test items. They constrain behavior, not how the code is built. `requirements.references.source_item` only defines a term.

No implementation roots were supplied. No structural obligation needs implementation evidence here, so I found no missing root. Whether tests cover the behavior is outside this assessment.

behavioral: The subject has two behavioral obligations. `habeas status` MUST display file, line and test name for each unmarked test. It MUST also exit successfully when it completes the report with those findings. The test `tests/coverage.rs#fn[status_reports_each_unmarked_test_and_exits_successfully]` covers both. I did not read the `project()` helper or the implementation.

- **Reporting each violation:** The test runs the real `habeas` binary with `status` on a project containing two unmarked tests. One is the `#[tokio::test] async fn ready` in `src/lib.rs`. The other is `#[test] fn another` in `src/other.rs`. It asserts that stdout contains a diagnostic with the file, the line, and the test name for each of them. These assertions cover the file, line and name for more than one finding, across different files and attribute forms.
- **Marked tests not reported:** In `src/other.rs`, the `marked` function carries a `{test}` annotation. The test asserts that stdout does not mention it.
- **Successful exit with findings:** `output.status.success()` is asserted while findings are present.
- **Clearing a finding:** After the marker is added to `src/lib.rs`, the test reruns `status`. It asserts a successful exit and that `ready` is no longer reported.

What counts as a violation, and which functions are test source items, belongs to `requirements.references.coverage.tests` and its definitions. That requirement is cited context, so I did not reassess it here. I found no unacknowledged gap.

text: :::{req} status.test_annotations
`habeas status` MUST display the file, line, and test name for each violation of
{cite}`requirements.references.coverage.tests`. The command MUST exit successfully
when it completes the report with these findings.
:::{req} coverage.tests
Every {term}`requirements.references.test_source_item` MUST carry one or more
`{test}` annotations in comments belonging to that item under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`.
:::{definition} source_item
:phrase: source item
A node in a project file’s outline, identified by the project-relative path
and an outline selector. For example, `src/auth.rs#fn[check_token]` identifies
a Rust function. The root node represents the whole file. A reference in a
comment belongs to the item that owns the comment under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`.
:::{definition} test_source_item
:phrase: test source item
A {term}`requirements.references.source_item` recognized as a test by Habeas.
In first-party Rust sources under {cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage.parsing`,
this is a function with `#[test]` or an attribute whose path ends in `test`,
such as `#[tokio::test]`. This includes functions in Cargo integration-test targets.
